entries.notes: The FIELD computation is validated: it runs, is finite on all free cells, and is correctly monotone (open > enclosed). The VISIBILITY MODEL is flagged: isovist_fields uses a thin int()-truncation ray march that is NOT the supercover test, so it leaks through diagonal walls and grazing partition corners — the exact S1 defect los.segment_is_free fixes but which isovist_fields does not call. See FINDING_isovist_visibility_march_2026-07-30.md. Recommended fix: route the per-ray occlusion through segment_is_free (or a supercover step).

entries.notes: Adapter -> PlanGrid -> isovist_fields runs correctly on real GT geometry: finite openness on 100% of free cells, plausible cell_m (~0.08 m) and free/obst fractions, fast (~1.5 s at grid_n=160). Caveat: Structured3D rooms are largely axis-aligned, so the visibility-march leak (previous entry) has small but nonzero impact here, concentrated at grazing corners; it would grow with diagonal/angled walls. Scale-up to more scenes is cheap.
